description: Reconstruction filter cap on mod 1-4 outputs
notes: 1k x 82nF = 1.94kHz. Real attenuation on the 3.6kHz ZOH image that a 15.9kHz corner ignores. FOUR not five: breath does not pass through the DAC and has its own 330nF (C-OUT-BREATH, ~480Hz). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.. 82nF C0G 50V EXISTS IN 1206: Murata GRM31C5C1H823JA01L, LCSC C97947 [ds MURATA-GRM31C5C1H823JA01L-82NF-C0G-1206.pdf]

description: Feedback leg (R2) of each mod channel's two-resistor network
notes: R2 of each channel. R2/R1 = k = 3, so gain = 1+k = EXACTLY 4 and the intercept is k x V_ref with V_ref = 3.3333V from the offset channel - which lands the window on exactly +-10.000V. EIGHT RESISTORS FOR FOUR CHANNELS, not sixteen: do not order a four-resistor difference-amp set. SPECIFIED 0.1 % (owner, 2026-10-01): worst case +-5.0mV of zero and -0.15/+0.15 percent of span at the op-amp output, mod-channels.md; at the jack, mod-jack-range. Same-sign parts cancel in the ratio, which is the reason for one series and TCR grade (R-MODGAIN-IN). YAGEO RT0805BRD0730KL, LCSC C728649

description: Input leg (R1) of each mod channel's two-resistor network
notes: R1 of each channel, and it goes to the SHARED buffered reference from DAC ch7, NOT to ground - that is what makes a CLR park every jack at 0V. Four, one per channel. It is the RATIO with R-MODGAIN-FB that has to hold, not either absolute value: SPECIFIED 0.1 % (owner, 2026-10-01), both values from ONE SERIES AND TCR GRADE, Yageo RT0805BRD07 (B = 0.1 %, D = 25 ppm/C [ds datasheets/discrete-and-power/YAGEO-RT-THIN-FILM-CHIP-RESISTOR-RT0805FRE0710KL.pdf p.2]), which holds the ratio to 0.2 % [calc] - two values cannot come off one reel.
